origin.description: Files in a directory of one R type.
origin.usage: list_files_with_type(dir, type, all.files = FALSE, full.names = TRUE, OS_subdirs = .OStype())

arguments.name: all.files
arguments.text: Include names that start with a dot.

arguments.name: full.names
arguments.text: Return paths instead of bare names.

arguments.name: OS_subdirs
arguments.text: OS-specific subdirectories included for code and docs.

origin.details: code uses R, r, S, s, q. demo uses R and r and then keeps names that start with a letter. code and docs also list a subdirectory named by R_OSTYPE, or unix.
origin.value: A character vector of names or paths.
origin.example: dir <- tempfile(); dir.create(dir); writeLines("z", file.path(dir, "a.R")); list_files_with_type(dir, "code", full.names = FALSE)

translation.description: Files in a directory of one R type.

arguments.name: all.files
arguments.text: Include names that start with a dot.

arguments.name: full.names
arguments.text: Return paths instead of bare names.

arguments.name: OS_subdirs
arguments.text: OS-specific subdirectories included for code and docs.

translation.details: The extension lists match R 4.5.0. When os_subdirs is omitted it is unix on this host, which is .OStype().
translation.value: A list of names or paths.
translation.example:
import os, tempfile
from tools import list_files_with_type
directory = tempfile.mkdtemp()
open(os.path.join(directory, "a.R"), "w").write("z\n")
print(list_files_with_type(directory, "code", full_names=False))
